solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Poet and novelist Beatle mithered dreadfully

parts.note: George Harrison was one of the four Beatles

indicators.note: done dreadfully, the letters are badly jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A literary type is irritated by a Beatle and complains about it in Northern dialect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mithered' is Northern English for bothered; here it is just fodder, and 'dreadfully' rearranges it into the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian writer of The Egoist published both verse (Modern Love) and novels.

clue.text: Those above helping with newspaper article on hair products

indicators.note: in a down answer, on means placed after, so the hair products come below the article

parts.note: The Guardian is a British national daily newspaper
an is the indefinite article
gels are styling products for hair

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece reviews hair-styling products.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Those above helping' is a playful way of describing heavenly protectors watching over people from on high.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiritual protectors are believed to watch over and assist people from heaven.

clue.text: Facing river in workplace

indicators.note: in means the river is placed inside the word built from work and place

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
a site is a place
the Po is Italy's longest river

explanation.surface: An office building faces onto a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'workplace' reads as one word, but it splits into 'work' and 'place', and the Italian river slots in between.
explanation.definitionFit: Something facing another thing stands across from it, on the other side.

clue.text: Good — a home win!

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: A football fan celebrates a home victory.
explanation.definitionFit: To win something is to obtain or acquire it, which is the verb sense here.

clue.text: See 1
Finished off going east out of city? I'd meant to go another way

indicators.note: going out of says the east letter departs from the city's name

parts.note: Exeter is a cathedral city in Devon
E is the compass abbreviation for east

indicators.note: to go another way the letters take a different route, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone excuses a wrong turn when leaving a city, saying they intended another route.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing one E from EXETER leaves EXTER; 'go another way' rearranges I'D MEANT into MINATED.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish off an enemy or pest is to kill it completely, to wipe it out.

clue.text: Heartbroken over the 1 down's charges, so the astronaut goes home

indicators.note: in a down answer, over means placed above, so the anagram comes first
broken means the letters of heart are smashed and reassembled

parts.note: 1 down is GUARDIAN, and a guardian's charges are wards

explanation.surface: A heartbroken guardian frets over children in their care, while a space traveller heads back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartbroken' is one word in the surface, but 'Heart' is the fodder and 'broken' the anagram signal. The 1-down reference is to GUARDIAN alone, not the full linked answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Heading towards our planet is the direction a returning spacefarer travels.

clue.text: First day of winter shortly? It's frozen over

indicators.note: winter's first day is 1st December, and shortly means abbreviated, so the date becomes DEC I

parts.note: the first day, written as a date, is the 1st, numeral I

explanation.surface: A forecaster warns that winter's first morning will bring a hard frost.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is an instruction: ICED written up, as a down entry is read from the bottom, gives DEC I, short for 1st December. 'It's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Covered with a layer of ice, as a pond or windscreen becomes in hard frost.

clue.text: Where rows regularly occur, hospital treated one extremely lucky man with these

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital on road signs and maps

indicators.note: treated means processed or worked on, so these letters are reshaped
extremely means taking the extreme ends of the word lucky

explanation.surface: A hospital patient got off lightly after treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rows' means rowing, not arguments: the Oxfordshire town hosts the Royal Regatta each summer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thames-side town is home to the famous Royal Regatta, the annual rowing event.

clue.text: A Disney film show? That's one that'll take care of the children

definitions.text: one that'll take care of the children

parts.note: Up is a 2009 Disney-Pixar animated film
to air something is to show or broadcast it

explanation.surface: A family asks whether a Disney film is showing, so the childminder can take the children.
explanation.definitionFit: A young foreign helper living with a family, minding the kids in return for board.

clue.text: Good person to encourage a swimmer

parts.note: a saint, abbreviated ST, is a very good person
to urge on is to encourage

explanation.surface: A kind-hearted coach cheers on a swimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a swimmer' looks like the person being encouraged, but it is the definition: a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: This large fish, source of caviar, is a swimming creature.

clue.text: New costly Micro model for one of the 19?

indicators.note: new means a fresh arrangement of the letters

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: A pricey new compact model is advertised.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 refers to the second word of 1/19 down; together with Hell's in front it names the famous biker gang.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Hell's gang named by 19 are bikers, so one of them rides a motorbike.

clue.text: Bit of dead wood

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for dead, as in genealogies
ash is a type of tree and its timber

explanation.surface: A splinter from a dead tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A small amount, as in a dash of milk, is a little bit.

clue.text: Woohoo! FA finally lost hearing here

indicators.note: finally lost says the FA, an O, is dropped from the end of Woohoo, leaving WOO HO

parts.note: FA (sweet Fanny Adams) means nothing, the letter O; woo means to court and HO is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A cheer goes up as the Football Association finally loses a case.
explanation.walkthrough: Translate the answer's halves: to court is to woo, and HO abbreviates house, giving WOO HO, which is Woohoo with its last O (FA, nothing) dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal hearing takes place in a building housing the law courts.

clue.text: One working closely with another barrel-maker has a roll-up

parts.note: a cooper makes barrels

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the word for roll is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a rota is a roll or list of duties

explanation.surface: A barrel-maker sits down for a hand-rolled cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roll-up' looks like a cigarette, but splits into 'roll' and the reversal signal 'up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who collaborates, working jointly with a partner towards a common end.

clue.text: Huge sort of telescope

definitions.meaning: enormous, as in a vast sum of money
a telescope for observing stars and planets

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from star-gazing: vast distances in space, and instruments for viewing the heavens.

clue.text: Ring a friend about rise of chart-topping intro to trumpet voluntary

parts.note: a ring is O-shaped

indicators.note: about means the ring and friend letters go around the rest

parts.note: a pal is a friend

indicators.note: the intro to a word is its opening letter
in a down answer, rise means reading upwards, backwards

parts.note: the record topping the chart is number one, NO I

explanation.surface: Ringing a pal about a trumpet piece that topped the charts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trumpet Voluntary' is a famous Baroque piece, but 'voluntary' is the definition. 'rise of' turns NO I (number one) into ION.
explanation.definitionFit: Something optional is left to one's free choice, done willingly, not compelled.

clue.text: See 8
Small tool, new, keeping groomed pandas spotlessly clean

indicators.note: keeping means holding the other letters inside

parts.note: a pick is a digging tool

indicators.note: groomed means tidied and rearranged

explanation.surface: A zookeeper uses a small new tool to groom pandas until they shine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small tool' looks like one gadget but is two pieces; 'keeping' wraps them and N round ANDSPA, the pandas rearranged by 'groomed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat and immaculately tidy is the idiomatic meaning of this fixed phrase.

clue.text: See 1
Don't go to bed in Cork?

definitions.meaning: stay awake late into the night
as a verb, to cork means to plug or seal a bottle; the question mark flags that it is not the Irish city

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cork' with a capital looks like the Irish city, but it is the verb, to plug.
explanation.definitionFit: One phrase means remaining awake late, the other means blocking an opening such as a bottle neck.

clue.text: Title from ballet — one that's opened at Christmas, seen by fan

indicators.note: seen by means placed beside, here with the fan coming first

parts.note: a nut is an enthusiast or fan
a Christmas cracker is pulled open at the dinner table

explanation.surface: A ballet fan sees a Christmas production.
explanation.walkthrough: A Christmas cracker is a paper tube pulled apart at British Christmas dinners, with a snap, a hat and a joke inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Tchaikovsky's famous ballet, traditionally staged at Christmas, bears this name.

clue.text: Off on a trip?

definitions.meaning: meat or game that has gone off is beginning to go bad

explanation.walkthrough: 'Off on a trip' reads as going on holiday; it splits into two separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is gamey, going bad; the other is drugged and intoxicated.

clue.text: Coming from England, a naturalised Irish singer

indicators.note: coming from means the letters are taken from within these words

explanation.surface: A singer from England has become naturalised as Irish.
explanation.definitionFit: The singer who won the 1970 Eurovision Song Contest for Ireland with All Kinds of Everything.

clue.text: Understanding how it feels to be a chimp, with endless tea drunk

indicators.note: drunk means the letters are reeling into a different order
endless means the final letter of tea is cut off

explanation.surface: Imagining life as a chimp at a tea party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts TEA to TE, and 'drunk' then rearranges A CHIMP with TE.
explanation.definitionFit: Able to share and appreciate another's feelings, which is what empathy is.

clue.text: Bottle shown by US detective

definitions.meaning: a wine bottle holding twice the standard amount
Thomas ..., the Hawaii private investigator in the TV series ..., P.I.

explanation.walkthrough: The detective is from the 1980s US television show set in Hawaii.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a double-size wine bottle; the other is the TV private eye played by Tom Selleck.

clue.text: Film from second Beatles era, with tap-dancing

indicators.note: dancing means the letters jig into a new order

explanation.surface: A documentary on a period of the Beatles' career featuring tap-dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tap-dancing' splits: 'tap' is fodder and 'dancing' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1958 movie based on Terence Rattigan's play, starring David Niven and Deborah Kerr.
